query: In conventional alloys, loss of toughness has long been associated with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation. By contrast, compositionally complex high-entropy alloys can suppress rapid grain coarsening and deleterious intermetallic formation and have shown favorable strength–ductility combinations and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement. These findings do not establish what governs possible toughness degradation in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy. Under the constraint of retaining a compositionally complex alloy suitable for demanding engineering service, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why brittle behavior emerges? Specify a controlled comparison that would distinguish the hypothesis from conventional-alloy expectations, predicted observations relative to the initial baseline, its service and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification outcome.

generation.hypothesis: Thermal aging treatments at intermediate temperatures induce enhanced L12 ordering in the FCC domains of the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA, forming jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries that promote planar slip and local stress concentration. This results in a non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile transition, where embrittlement at ~600°C is followed by ductile recovery at higher temperatures (e.g., ~750°C) due to suppressed ordering and the formation of ductile transition zones.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA in as-cast state (FCC + B2 phases)
generation.intervention: Thermal aging treatments applied at intermediate temperatures (~600°C for embrittlement and ~750°C for ductile recovery)
generation.conditions: Aging regime within a temperature window approximately 550–750°C where ordering kinetics and phase boundary morphology evolution are active
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced L12 ordering in FCC domains (approaching perfect Ni3Al stoichiometry) combined with the formation of jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries
generation.mechanism: The combination of elevated anti-phase boundary energy (APBE) and a higher elastic modulus in the ordered domains restricts cross-slip, favoring planar slip. The jagged phase boundary tips act as stress concentrators that trigger local plastic instability and embrittlement. At higher temperatures, reduced ordering and the development of more ductile transition zones along the phase boundaries restore ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: A non-monotonic transition in toughness: maximum embrittlement (minimal ductility) at ~600°C aging due to peak L12 ordering and jagged phase boundary density; subsequent recovery of ductility at ~750°C when ordering diminishes and ductile transition zones form.
generation.baseline: Conventional alloys typically exhibit thermal embrittlement via grain-boundary impurity segregation leading to a monotonic decrease in toughness, without the non-monotonic recovery observed here.
generation.boundary: Service temperatures below ~550°C will not trigger the transition, the embrittlement window occurs between 550°C and 750°C, and temperatures above 750°C yield ductile recovery.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative shift in ductility and the exact temperature boundaries require further experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform thermal aging experiments on as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 HEA samples at various temperatures (e.g., 550°C, 600°C, 750°C) and characterize the evolution of phase ordering and phase boundary morphology using high-resolution TEM or TKD. Concurrently, assess dislocation behavior and crack initiation at these interfaces during mechanical loading.
measurements: TEM/TKD imaging to document L12 ordering intensity and morphology of B2/FCC phase boundaries
In situ mechanical testing to measure ductility and pinpoint the onset of plastic instability
Observation of dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation specifically at jagged phase boundary tips
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the materials do not exhibit a non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile transition (i.e., if no embrittlement is observed at ~600°C followed by recovery at ~750°C) or if the microstructural analysis fails to show enhanced L12 ordering and jagged phase boundaries correlated with dislocation pile-ups at embrittlement temperatures, then the hypothesis is rejected.
